blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Biodiversity increases along a latitudinal gradient from the poles toward the equator.
Tropical rainforests harbor more than half of all species on Earth.
Coral reefs are widely designated as the 'rainforests of the sea'.
Islands display high species endemism but are highly vulnerable to ecological disturbance.
High tropical biodiversity is driven by stable historical climate, high primary productivity from solar energy, long growing seasons, and complex habitats.

blocks.content: • Stable climate over millions of years.

items: Focus on the 4 primary drivers of tropical species richness: stable climate, high solar energy/productivity, long growing seasons, and niche specialization.
Distinguish between spatial patterns: Latitudinal gradient applies from poles to equator, whereas altitudinal zonation applies to mountain regions.
Remember that island ecosystems are characterized by high endemism combined with high vulnerability.

blocks.content: • High solar energy leading to greater primary productivity.
